newsitem.title: Jordan: Hamas warns of anger at Israeli building plans.
newsitem.headline: Hamas warns of anger at Israeli building plans.

text.p: The Islamic resistance movement Hamas said on Thursday Israel's decision to build Jewish homes in Arab East Jerusalem was "very dangerous" and warned that Israel may not be able to contain Palestinian anger.
"The Palestinian people feel they have a knife on their hearts and they will want to express their pain with strong demonstrations," Hamas spokesman Ibrahim Ghosheh told Reuters.
"This is a very important and dangerous decision," he said.
Suicide bombers from the military wing of Hamas, which rejects the Palestinian-Israeli self-rule deal as a sell-out, killed dozens of Israelis in a series of attacks a year ago.

Ghosheh said he expected a muted response from Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and other Arab leaders to the Israeli decision to build 6,500 houses for Jews in Jabal Abu Ghneim, called Har Homa by Israel.
"It seems there are strict orders from Arafat not to confront the Israelis," he said.
"But Arab and Moslem people will not accept this step and will try to express their rejection," he said, adding that anger could spill over during Friday weekly Moslem prayers.
"Tomorrow is Friday -- all the mosques will be surrounded by guards, but no one can tell what will happen."
Ghosheh said if the building plans were carried out, Israelis would have effectively surrounded Arab East Jerusalem with its own settlements.
"This means complete and total closure around Arab East Jerusalem," he said.
Israel says all of Jerusalem is its capital. Palestinians say East Jerusalem, captured by Israeli forces during the 1967 Middle East war, will form the capital of their future state.

"In the near future maybe the Palestinian Authority and Israel will be able to control the (Palestinian) reaction, but the bulldozers will start in two weeks, and who can say what will happen" Ghosheh said.
